Where it began

Saqlain Mushtaq was born in Lahore on 29 December 1976. He never played cricket at school. Instead he joined the second eleven of Zareef Memorial Cricket Club at 13. One of his elder brothers, Sibtain, went on to play first-class cricket for Lahore. At 14 he moved on to Govt. M.A.O. College in Lahore, and the college won its championship in each of his three years there.

He always wanted to bowl off-spin rather than fast. He made his first-class debut at 17 in 1994–95 and took 52 wickets in that first season.

The player

His first Test came in September 1995 against Sri Lanka at Peshawar. Over the next nine years he played 49 Tests and took 208 wickets at 29.83, with 13 five-wicket innings and three matches of ten wickets or more. His best, 8 for 164, came against England at Lahore in 2000.

The series everyone recalls is India in 1999. In the first Test he took five wickets in each innings and dismissed Sachin Tendulkar for 136 with India just 17 runs from victory, and Pakistan won. He did the same again in the next match at Delhi, finishing the series with 20 wickets and the player of the series award.

In one-day cricket he was even more of a handful. He took 288 wickets in ODIs, two hat-tricks against Zimbabwe, and 69 in the calendar year 1997 alone.

What made him special

Saqlain is credited with inventing the doosra, a ball delivered with an off-spinner's action that turns the other way. Batsmen had to guess, and many guessed wrong. Plenty of spinners took it up after him. At Surrey he kept experimenting and came up with another variation he called the teesra, though little is known about how it worked.

With the bat he was not often a worry for bowlers, averaging 14.48. That makes his one Test hundred all the sweeter: an unbeaten 101 against New Zealand at Christchurch in March 2001.

Away from the middle

Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year in 2000. He played eight seasons for Surrey, from 1997 to 2004, and later spent time with Sussex and in club cricket in England, including a first summer with Old Whitgiftians that brought him 64 wickets.

Coaching came naturally to him. England brought him in as a spin consultant in 2016, and between 2021 and 2022 he was head coach of the Pakistan team.

And finally

Few bowlers can say they added a word to cricket's language. Saqlain gave the game the doosra, then followed it with the teesra, whose name means the third one. Batsmen of his day could be forgiven for hoping he would stop counting there.
